clue.text: One renounces all dignity in coat woven with braid

indicators.note: woven means the letters of the two words are interlaced into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A ceremonial figure gives up all dignity, dressed in a braided coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woven' scrambles COAT and BRAID together; 'in' and 'with' are link words. 'All dignity' here means high office, such as a throne.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abdicates gives up a throne or high office, renouncing its rank.

clue.text: Strength of current in wild rampage around head of Euphrates

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters surround the next piece
wild tells us the letters of rampage run riot into another order
head of means take only the opening letter of the river's name

explanation.surface: A river in flood rampages wildly, its current immensely strong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' turns RAMPAGE into AMPRAGE, and 'around' wraps it round E, the first letter of Euphrates.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrical current is measured in amps, so its strength is its amperage.

clue.text: Rustic English style of architecture

definitions.meaning: a broad country dialect of English speech
one of the classical Greek orders of columns

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a broad country dialect and the plainest of the classical column orders.

clue.text: With equal power, act against and bar the rest!

parts.note: a bar in a pub or shop is a counter
the rest of a sum owed is the balance

explanation.surface: A rallying cry to match force with force and shut out everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a verb meaning exclude, but it is the noun: a counter. 'and' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To offset a force with an equal weight or power working the other way.

clue.text: The first defence of disloyalty?

indicators.note: first means take only the opening letter of the word The

parts.note: a defence offered for an action is a reason or justification

explanation.surface: Asks whether disloyalty is the best line of defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The first' gives T; 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Betraying one's country or sovereign is the gravest form of disloyalty.

clue.text: New sort on curious platform

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits above the next
New means the letters of sort are made into a fresh order

parts.note: the word sort supplies the letters to be rearranged
rum is British slang for odd or curious

explanation.surface: Something novel and strange appears on a stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges SORT to ROST, and 'on' sets it above RUM, an old British word for strange.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised stand for a speaker is a platform.

clue.text: Mark has to replace billiard ball

definitions.meaning: a mark is a small dot or stain
in billiards a ball is put back on its marked place on the table

explanation.definitionFit: A dot or blemish is a small mark, and in billiards and snooker a ball is put back on its marked place.

clue.text: Formality of PC 10 until appointed?

indicators.note: appointed means set out in a new arrangement, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: 10 read as the letters I and O

explanation.surface: A policeman's punctual shift: PC 10 is on duty until a set time.
explanation.walkthrough: The figures 10 are read as the letters IO; 'appointed' (arranged) scrambles PC, IO and UNTIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine point of etiquette or correct conduct is a formality.

clue.text: Language of one in business

indicators.note: in means the letter for one goes inside the word for business

parts.note: trade is commerce or business
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: The jargon used by someone working in commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Language' means a torrent of angry words, as in 'mind your language'.
explanation.definitionFit: A long angry speech is abusive language poured out at length.

clue.text: Admire skill and decency

parts.note: to admire is to respect
skill is ability

explanation.surface: Praise for someone both talented and well behaved.
explanation.definitionFit: Being proper and socially acceptable amounts to decency.

clue.text: Lost to view in deeper dungeon

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the words deeper dungeon

explanation.surface: A prisoner vanishes in the lowest dungeon.
explanation.definitionFit: A French borrowing for something hidden away out of sight.

clue.text: Person from Hartford on Hertford

parts.note: both towns lie in the east of their countries: Hartford in Connecticut, Hertford north of London

explanation.surface: A traveller from the American Hartford turns up in the English Hertford.
explanation.walkthrough: Hartford is in New England on the US east coast; Hertford, pronounced the same way, is a county town in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone from either town hails from the eastern side of their country.

clue.text: Details of Roman thing outside French city

indicators.note: outside means the Latin word wraps round the French one

parts.note: res is the Latin word for a thing
cite is the French word for city

explanation.surface: Particulars of a Roman artefact found outside a French town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Details' is a verb here, to list one by one. 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To detail is to list items in turn, as one repeats a list aloud.

clue.text: Alleged to have been established in tall grass

indicators.note: in means the word for established goes inside the plant

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wet ground
to put something is to set or establish it

explanation.surface: A claim that something was founded among tall reeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to have been' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something supposed or generally believed is said to be so, alleged.

clue.text: Grand, enormously large epicurean

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand
astronomical means vast, like distances in space

explanation.surface: A lavish gourmet with enormous appetites.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to fine eating, as an epicure enjoys.

clue.text: Suggestion of bad vibes?

definitions.meaning: a feeling of mistrust about someone

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a slight hint or trace and an uneasy sense of mistrust.

clue.text: Grantees free to separate

indicators.note: free means the letters of Grantees are loosened into a new order

explanation.surface: People granted land are freed to split up.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate or drive apart people who were close is to separate them.

clue.text: One can not win large chips with so little money!

definitions.text: One can not win large chips with so little money!

parts.words: One can not win large chips with so little money!
parts.note: a gambler's lament about stakes too tiny to matter, read as tiny fried potatoes

explanation.surface: A gambler grumbles that a tiny stake will never win big chips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chips' suggests casino tokens, but the answer's phrase is about trivial sums, pictured as little potatoes.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means something trivial or an insignificant sum of money.

clue.text: Man, according to some consumers, dragging over Berkshire?

parts.note: something dragging on is long and tedious
the Berkshire is a breed of pig

explanation.surface: A man dragging something across the English county of Berkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Berkshire is an English county, but here it is the pig breed named after it. 'some consumers' are cannibals.
explanation.definitionFit: A grim term said to be used by cannibals for human flesh, likening it to pork.

clue.text: To return greeting in play

indicators.note: return means the word To is read backwards

parts.note: hello is a greeting

explanation.surface: Coming back to say hello at the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns TO into OT; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragedy of the Moor of Venice is a play.

clue.text: Dreamy Jack roused to ecstasy

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, abbreviated AB for able seaman
to be sent is to be thrilled into rapture

explanation.surface: A sailor in a dreamy state, carried away with joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Absent-minded and lost in thought is dreamy.

clue.text: Country mind if it is imported?

indicators.note: imported means brought in, so one word is put inside the other

parts.note: the brain is the mind

explanation.surface: A nation that cares little whether goods are brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mind' looks like a verb (object to), but it is the noun BRAIN; 'if' and 'is' link.
explanation.definitionFit: Great Britain is a country.

clue.text: Greater shock apparently, the more alarming it is

definitions.meaning: having a bigger shock of hair, so more hirsute
hairy is slang for frightening, so this is its comparative

explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of a word meaning both shaggy-haired and frightening.

clue.text: Architect's handle popular with one on the move?

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
the Roman numeral for one is I
on the go means busy, on the move

explanation.surface: A busy architect who is well liked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handle' is slang for a name: the first name of Inigo Jones, the English architect.
explanation.definitionFit: A handle is a person's name, here the first name of a famous English architect.

clue.text: Work in special constitution of one such church

definitions.note: a noun phrase defining an adjective: belonging to a church governed by bishops

indicators.note: in means the work goes inside the rearranged letters
constitution means make-up, so the letters of special are made up afresh

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Work on a special constitution for a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constitution of' rearranges SPECIAL to make ESICAL, which wraps round OP.
explanation.definitionFit: A church governed by bishops is described this way.

clue.text: A sovereign bound to go round?

definitions.text: A sovereign bound to go round?

parts.words: A sovereign bound to go round?
parts.note: in Greek myth a king of the Lapiths was bound to a wheel turning for ever

explanation.surface: Looks like a gold coin destined to circulate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sovereign' suggests the British gold coin, which would 'go round' as money, but it is a king tied to a wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: A mythical Greek king punished by Zeus by being tied to an ever-turning wheel.

clue.text: Spanish wine some guys keep down

definitions.meaning: a deep red wine from Spain, now rare
guy ropes hold canvas shelters to the ground

explanation.definitionFit: The word names an old red wine from Spain and a canvas shelter held down by guy ropes.

clue.text: Crow nest in a small, untidy room?

parts.note: to crow is to glory or exult
a hole can be a nest or den

explanation.surface: A crow builds its nest in a tiny messy room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crow' looks like the bird, but it is the verb, to exult; 'in a' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A cubbyhole where junk is stuffed out of sight is a messy little room.
